{{Nihongo|'''Masaaki Yamada'''|山田雅章|Yamada Masaaki|4=born August 9, 1942 in [[Japan]]|lead=yes}}<ref>{{Cite book|last=Gale Group.|title=American men & women of science.|date=2004|publisher=Gale|oclc=1082415302}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.friendsofutokyo.org/ja/%e5%b1%b1%e7%94%b0%e9%9b%85%e7%ab%a0%e7%90%86%e4%ba%8b%e3%82%92%e6%96%b0futi%e7%90%86%e4%ba%8b%e9%95%b7%e3%81%ab%e9%81%b8%e5%87%ba%e3%80%81%e6%a1%91%e9%96%93%e9%9b%84%e4%b8%80%e9%83%8e%e7%90%86/|title=山田雅章理事を新FUTI理事長に選出、桑間雄一郎理事が副理事長に|date=2015-10-17|website=Friends of UTokyo, Inc.|language=ja|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref> is a Japanese [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] physicist known for his studies on [[magnetic reconnection]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yamada|first1=Masaaki|last2=Kulsrud|first2=Russell|last3=Ji|first3=Hantao|date=2010|title=Magnetic reconnection|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=82|issue=1|pages=603–664|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.82.603|bibcode=2010RvMP...82..603Y}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zweibel|first1=Ellen G.|last2=Yamada|first2=Masaaki|date=2009|title=Magnetic Reconnection in Astrophysical and Laboratory Plasmas|journal=Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics|volume=47|issue=1|pages=291–332|doi=10.1146/annurev-astro-082708-101726|bibcode=2009ARA&A..47..291Z}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yamada|first1=Masaaki|last2=Ji|first2=Hantao|last3=Hsu|first3=Scott|last4=Carter|first4=Troy|last5=Kulsrud|first5=Russell|last6=Bretz|first6=Norton|last7=Jobes|first7=Forrest|last8=Ono|first8=Yasushi|last9=Perkins|first9=Francis|date=1997|title=Study of driven magnetic reconnection in a laboratory plasma|journal=Physics of Plasmas|volume=4|issue=5|pages=1936–1944|doi=10.1063/1.872336|bibcode=1997PhPl....4.1936Y|issn=1070-664X|url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc679550/}}</ref>

Yamada obtained a bachelor's degree in applied physics at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1966 and a master's degree in nuclear engineering in 1968, and received a doctorate in physics from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]] in 1973. He was then at [[Princeton University]] and from 1978 at its [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] (PPPL), where he and [[Robert Ellis (physicist)|Robert Ellis]] led the development of the [[Spheromak]] S-1, a compact toroidal device for plasma confinement from 1978 to 1988, which was investigated for some time as an alternative to the [[Tokamak]].<ref>Kees Bol, Harold P. Furth, Melvin B. Gottlieb, Lyman Spitzer, Thomas H. Stix, Masaaki Yamada, James A. Van Allen; Robert A. Ellis Jr. ''Physics Today'' 1 March 1991; 44 (3): 86–88. https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2810048</ref> He has been a Principal Research Physicist at the PPPL since 1982 (2015 he is a Distinguished Laboratory Research Fellow). Since the beginning of the 1990s, he has been leading a research program to research [[magnetic reconnection]] at the PPPL ([[Magnetic Reconnection Experiment]], MRX) with applications both on [[Magnetic confinement fusion|fusion plasmas]] and in [[astrophysics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pppl.gov/news/2016/09/physicist-masaaki-yamadas-pioneering-career-pppl|title=Physicist Masaaki Yamada's pioneering career at PPPL {{!}} Princeton Plasma Physics Lab|website=www.pppl.gov|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1985, received the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] from APS in 2002<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Yamada&first_nm=Masaaki&year=2002|title=2002 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref> and the Kaul Prize from Princeton University in 2003. In 2015, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for his research on reconnection and as a pioneer in laboratory plasma physics for astrophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Yamada&first_nm=Masaaki&year=2015|title=2015 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref> He has published over 200 scientific publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=s9pxxTYAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|title=Masaaki Yamada - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2020-02-27}}</ref>

He was a visiting professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]], the [[University of Tokyo]] and [[Kyoto University]].
